title: Absolute deviation of a standardized biased sign
statement: Let $0<p<1$, and choose a random sign $X\in\{-1,1\}$ with probabilities $\mathbb{P}(X=1)=1-p$ and $\mathbb{P}(X=-1)=p$. Its mean is $1-2p$ and its standard deviation is $\sigma=\sqrt{4p(1-p)}$; the expected absolute value of $(X-(1-2p))/\sigma$ is $\sigma$.
